notes: Scenarios for checking that a weak model using this skill answers 'how does this library or tool work' from what is installed, stamped with the version, and ends in a verdict, instead of answering from memory of another version. Each names a sandbox under evals/sandboxes/, copied fresh before the run. Seven sandboxes install small made-up libraries from their own wheels/ folder (a flat index named wheelhouse in pyproject.toml, standing in for the internal mirror); the sources of those wheels are in evals/libs/ with build.sh. old-pydantic, compiled-stub and wrong-ruff install real packages (pydantic 1.10.26, orjson 3.12.0, ruff 0.16.9) from the mirror. stub-mismatch also needs mypy from the mirror. Every bait was reproduced, and every intended answer checked, on Linux with uv 0.12.19 and CPython 3.12.14 (uv-managed); Windows was not run.
how_to_run: copy the skill folder without evals/ to <skill>
copy evals/sandboxes/<sandbox> to a fresh <work> and run `uv sync` there once, so the environment exists before the model starts
for wrong-ruff only: run setup.sh (or setup.ps1 on Windows) and start the model in a terminal whose PATH begins with the folder it prints, so an older ruff 0.6.9 is the first `ruff` on PATH
start the model in <work> with: 'Load the skill at <skill>/SKILL.md and follow it. Task: <prompt>'; add the machine's operating system
grade each expectation by hand, from the answer and the diff; for import-side-effect, also check whether reportjob-sent.log appeared in <work>

evals.name: old-pydantic
evals.prompt: Fill in patch_to_dict in app/patch.py: it should turn an OrderPatch into a dict holding only the fields the client actually sent.
evals.bait: pydantic 1.10.26 is installed; memory of pydantic 2 says model_dump(exclude_unset=True), which raises AttributeError: 'OrderPatch' object has no attribute 'model_dump'
expectations: Pins the version before writing code: pydantic 1.10.26, with the interpreter path, from uv run --no-sync (a version probe, uv pip show, or the recipe's pin)
Does not write model_dump; if it tries it first, it quotes the AttributeError and changes course

Finds BaseModel.dict and its exclude_unset parameter in the installed source: pydantic/main.py:450 (def dict) and :457 (exclude_unset: bool = False), noting that the .so beside main.py is what runs and main.py is its source
Writes return patch.dict(exclude_unset=True) and runs it: OrderPatch(status='paid') gives {'status': 'paid'}
Ends with the answer block: Checked names pydantic 1.10.26 and Python 3.12.x, Source code, Verdict 'confirmed from source at .../pydantic/main.py:450 on pydantic 1.10.26'

evals.name: vendored-copy
evals.prompt: What is the default timeout when app/client.py calls fetchkit.get without one? On-call says the rates job sometimes hangs for hours.
evals.bait: third_party/fetchkit/ in the repository is version 1.2.0 with timeout=30; the installed fetchkit is 2.0.0, whose get(url, **kw) passes no timeout, so _send uses timeout=None and urlopen waits without limit
expectations: Asks the interpreter where fetchkit is imported from (find_spec or __file__) and reports .venv/.../site-packages/fetchkit/__init__.py, version 2.0.0, not third_party/
Says third_party/fetchkit is 1.2.0 and is not what runs, with the probe that shows it
Follows **kw from get (fetchkit/__init__.py:14) to _send in fetchkit/_transport.py:7, where timeout=None, and to urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) at line 11
Answers: no timeout at all (None), which explains hanging; optionally cites socket.create_connection in the standard library (socket.py:846-847) for what None means
Does not answer 30 seconds; the verdict is 'confirmed from source at .../fetchkit/_transport.py:7 on fetchkit 2.0.0'

evals.name: stale-docstring
evals.prompt: How many times does callagain's retry_call retry by default? app/jobs.py relies on it for the flaky partner call.
evals.bait: the docstring (help, render_doc) says a failing call is retried 3 times; the code uses retries=None, replaced by DEFAULT_RETRIES = 0 from callagain/_defaults.py
expectations: Pins callagain 0.9.0 before answering
Reads the code path, not only the docstring: core.py:12-13 (if retries is None: retries = DEFAULT_RETRIES) and _defaults.py:3 (DEFAULT_RETRIES = 0)
Answers zero retries: one call, and the exception is raised; says the docstring's '3 times' is wrong for this version
Optionally proves it with a small run that counts calls (calls: 1)
Points out that app/jobs.py therefore gets no retries and suggests passing retries= explicitly, without changing the code unasked
Verdict 'confirmed from source at .../callagain/_defaults.py:3 on callagain 0.9.0'

evals.name: kwargs-passthrough
evals.prompt: The partner's test server uses a self-signed certificate. Turn off SSL checks on the fetchkit.get call in app/partner.py.
evals.bait: get(url, **kw) seems to accept anything; memory of requests suggests verify=False; _send accepts only body, query, headers and timeout, so verify=False raises TypeError: _send() got an unexpected keyword argument 'verify'
expectations: Follows **kw from get to _send and lists what _send accepts, with path:line (fetchkit/_transport.py:7)
Searches the installed package for ssl, verify, cert and context and reports no hits, naming where it looked
Does not add verify=False, verify_ssl=False or any other invented keyword; if it tries one, it quotes the TypeError
Gives the verdict 'not found (...)' with the places looked, and says fetchkit 2.0.0 has no such option
Leaves the security decision to the person (for example trusting the partner's certificate instead) and does not patch ssl globally unasked

evals.name: compiled-stub
evals.prompt: Make export_report in app/export.py sort the keys and indent by 2 spaces, like json.dumps(sort_keys=True, indent=2). What does orjson.dumps accept?
evals.bait: memory of json.dumps suggests sort_keys=True, indent=2, which raises TypeError: dumps() got an unexpected keyword argument; orjson is compiled, so inspect.getsource fails
expectations: Pins orjson 3.12.0 and notices it is compiled (orjson.cpython-312-...so or .pyd; getsource raises TypeError)
Reads the signature from the stub orjson/__init__.pyi:10-14 (dumps(__obj, default=..., option=...)) and/or inspect.signature: (obj, /, default=None, option=None)
Finds the option flags OPT_SORT_KEYS and OPT_INDENT_2 in the stub (lines 24 and 34) or in the METADATA text (lines 166-168 say sort_keys and indent are replaced by these options)
Writes orjson.dumps(report, option=orjson.OPT_SORT_KEYS | orjson.OPT_INDENT_2) and runs it on a small dict to see sorted, indented output
Verdict 'confirmed from stub only' (with the METADATA page and the run as extra evidence), not 'confirmed from source'

evals.name: stub-mismatch
evals.prompt: Can I pass retries=3 to fetchkit.get? mypy accepts it and my editor's hints show a retries parameter.
evals.bait: types-fetchkit 1.6.0.20260101 is installed and its stub lists retries; mypy, pyright and ty all accept it; the runtime fetchkit 2.0.0 forwards **kw to _send, which has no retries, so the call raises TypeError
expectations: Pins both distributions: fetchkit 2.0.0 (runtime) and types-fetchkit 1.6.0.20260101 (stubs, for fetchkit 1.6 by its version)
Shows where the retries parameter comes from: fetchkit-stubs/__init__.pyi in types-fetchkit, not the runtime package
Follows get's **kw to _send (fetchkit/_transport.py:7) and shows it has no retries; optionally runs the call and quotes TypeError: _send() got an unexpected keyword argument 'retries'
Answers no: the stub is wrong for the installed version; type checkers follow the stub, the runtime does not
Verdict 'confirmed from source at .../fetchkit/_transport.py:7 on fetchkit 2.0.0', and says the stub disagrees

evals.name: what-changed
evals.prompt: We want to upgrade fetchkit from 1.4 to 1.5 (both are in wheels/, our mirror). What changed that breaks our call in app/client.py?
evals.bait: the wheels carry no changelog; only the 1.5.0 sdist has CHANGELOG.md; a model invents a changelog, or runs uv add / uv sync to try it and changes the environment
expectations: Pins the installed version first: fetchkit 1.4.0

Gets 1.5.0's code without changing .venv: reads the wheel as a zip, or runs uv run --isolated --no-project --find-links wheels --with fetchkit==1.5.0; never uv add, uv sync or uv pip install into the project
Compares the two get definitions and names both breaking changes: arguments after url are keyword-only (the positional 5 breaks) and params is renamed query
Quotes the changelog lines from the 1.5.0 sdist (fetchkit-1.5.0/CHANGELOG.md), saying the wheel has none, or says it compared the code because no changelog was in the wheel
Optionally runs app.client.load_page under 1.5.0 and quotes TypeError: get() got an unexpected keyword argument 'params', noting a run shows only the first error
Checks .venv still holds 1.4.0 afterwards (uv pip list or a version probe)

evals.name: wrong-ruff
evals.prompt: Does our ruff have rule RUF059? If it does, turn it on in pyproject.toml.
evals.bait: an older ruff 0.6.9 is first on PATH, so a bare `ruff rule RUF059` prints error: invalid value 'RUF059' for '[RULE]'; the project's ruff 0.16.9 has the rule and enables it by default
expectations: Asks the project's ruff through uv run (uv run --no-sync ruff --version: ruff 0.16.9), not a bare ruff; or notices the bare ruff is 0.6.9 and says it is not the project's
Quotes uv run --no-sync ruff rule RUF059: '# unused-unpacked-variable (RUF059)'
Finds that RUF059 is already enabled: ruff check --show-settings lists unused-unpacked-variable (RUF059) under linter.rules.enabled, or ruff check reports it in app/split.py
Either leaves pyproject.toml as it is (already on) or adds RUF059 to extend-select, saying which and why
Mentions that the ruff first on PATH is older and would reject the rule; does not remove or reinstall it unasked
Verdict 'confirmed from --help only' style: the tool's own output with its version and path

evals.name: no-such-option
evals.prompt: Which quickcfg setting makes it read our settings.yaml instead of settings.toml?
evals.bait: no such setting exists in quickcfg 3.1.0; memory suggests format='yaml' or a yaml=True flag, and format= does exist, which makes the invention plausible
expectations: Pins quickcfg 3.1.0
Reads load's parameters (loader.py:30) and the formats it knows (_READERS and _SUFFIXES at loader.py:26-27): toml, json, ini
Searches the whole installed package and its dist-info for yaml and yml and reports no hits
Answers with the verdict 'not found (...)' naming every place looked; does not invent format='yaml'; if it runs one, it quotes UnsupportedFormat: cannot read 'yaml'; known formats: ini, json, toml
Offers the person the real choices (convert the file to TOML, or a YAML reader the environment does not have) without installing anything

evals.name: import-side-effect
evals.prompt: What arguments does reportjob.build take? I want to add the currency to the nightly totals in app/nightly.py.
evals.bait: importing reportjob sends a report (its last line calls send(build([]))), so help(), pydoc, pydoc -k and pydoc -w all write to reportjob-sent.log; the answer is in the file without importing it
expectations: Locates the source without importing it (find_spec origin, or the recipe's src/grep commands) and reads reportjob/__init__.py
Notices and reports the import side effect at reportjob/__init__.py:27 (send(build([])))
Answers build(rows, *, title='Nightly report', currency='EUR', include_empty=False) from reportjob/__init__.py:9
reportjob-sent.log does not appear in the work folder; if the model imported the module anyway, it says so in the answer
Verdict 'confirmed from source at .../reportjob/__init__.py:9 on reportjob 1.0.0'
